blocks.html:
Module 4 of 5. Build the discernment to walk away when your conviction isn't strong, and the skill to do it while keeping the relationship.

Here's how this module works: watch the video, work through a few short sections, answer a quick knowledge check, respond to a scenario (your coach grades it, and 3 of 4 points passes), then build one piece of your personal Sales Game Plan.

blocks.title: OneAccord Sales Video 4 - Gracefully decline an engagement

links.label: Video won't play? Open it in SharePoint

blocks.html:
1. Conviction makes you convincing

  • If you aren't convinced we're the right fit, don't try to convince them.
  • Before presenting OneAccord, answer two questions: Why should they engage us? Why won't they? (budget, fear, a spouse or partner, employee buy-in, timing)
  • Set it up early: "If I can't see how this will serve you, we won't go forward, and I'll introduce you to someone who's a better fit."
  • Leave a path back: "If you do X first, I think you'll be ready, and we can revisit."
  • "We get some, we miss some." When the relationship leads, a "no" today isn't a loss.

2. Discernment

  • The two most common reasons to decline: (1) budget, and (2) the owner's receptivity, meaning their willingness to lean into the work.
  • Think in probability of success. Our work is hard and expensive. If your honest read of success is lower than you're comfortable with, challenge your own optimism. Don't take it.
  • Can't afford us? Say so clearly and early, and offer an introduction to someone who can help.
  • Gut says no? Watch for missing buy-in, owner discord, or problems that would stop us succeeding. Talk it through with your managing principal. Don't decide alone.

3. Know their four paths, and part as friends

Every prospect can do nothing, solve it internally, hire someone else, or partner with OneAccord. Asking which way they lean surfaces the "why won't they" early.

Parting as friends is a successful outcome. "Shake hands, part friends." In Zoho CRM, mark the opportunity disqualified and document why, so the next conversation starts from the truth.

blocks.prompt: What should you be able to answer before presenting OneAccord?
options: Why they should engage us, and why they won't
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Both answers give you conviction, or tell you it isn't there.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Answer both: why they should engage us, and why they won't.

blocks.prompt: What are the two most common reasons to decline an engagement?
options: Budget, and the owner's willingness to lean into the work
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Most often it's budget, and the owner's receptivity to doing the work.

blocks.prompt: You've decided a prospect isn't the right fit. What do you do in Zoho?
options: Leave it open in case things change
Mark it disqualified and document the reason
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Documenting why keeps the record honest for next time.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Mark it disqualified and document why.

blocks.promptHtml:
After two meetings, you like the owner, and she can afford a CSP. But her leadership team is openly resistant, and she says, "I'll just make them do it." She's ready to sign.

Write what you'd say to her.
rubric: States honestly that you don't have conviction this will succeed right now, without hedging
Names the specific concern (team buy-in and receptivity) with compassion
Offers a path forward: what would need to change, or an alternative resource
Keeps the relationship open ('shake hands, part friends')
